environment.description: Chromium from Playwright on the production build under /getmath/, cold cache (a new browser context for every run), viewport 1280 by 800. Network: 150 ms round trip, 1600 kbit/s down, 750 kbit/s up (the slow 4G profile of Lighthouse), set through the Chrome DevTools Protocol. Processor: 4 times slower. Each run loads the page, waits for the interaction to start and for 1 second, presses 30 arrow keys on a handle, then drags it round a circle in 40 pointer moves. Arrow response is the time from the input to the next paint: Event Timing for the keyboard worst (it only reports events over 16 ms, in steps of 8 ms), and the event to the first frame and the task after it for the other three, because Event Timing does not cover pointer moves. The page weight counts bytes as the preview server sends them, without compression, so GitHub Pages sends less.

lcp.label: Largest contentful paint
lcp.why: About 2 times the runner's median of 436 ms and below the public 'good' guidance of 2500 ms. The developer machine's slowest run was 740 ms.

cls.label: Cumulative layout shift
cls.why: The page does not shift at all (0 in every run, in both places). 0.02 is well below the public 'good' guidance of 0.1 and still lets a real shift of the page fail.
